detail: 5 graph calls; 4 txns in episode window, 7 memory cases, 3 rare devices

rationale: The flagged item is a single online purchase of $599.94 (amount_z 3.57, 4.52x the card's 180d mean and above the card's prior maximum of $550.03) from a device never seen on this account and flagged 'New', in a billing region (327) with zero history on the card. That is pattern 3 shape, but only one online transaction, and this cardholder is unusually device-diverse (39 devices over 68 txns), so the 'New device' flag alone is weak. Two prior confirmed card_not_present_new_device frauds on this very card (CC-3886, CC-0615) raise the prior meaningfully, while CC-1313 and the semantically similar cases show this customer/population also generates cleared travel alerts. The rare device (8 cards all-time) shows only 1 card in the window, and the long fraud lists attached to linked cards come via 'Windows | Windows 7 | chrome 65.0 | 1280x1024', a common profile (44 cards all-time, 26 in window) that is not in this card's history, so no shared-origin conclusion is supported. Under R1 (probability below 0.70, essentially one anomalous transaction) I verified with the cardholder before recommending a block.
